sowhat.text: Stock-for-stock energy deals and a $5.7B sponsor-linked take-private show M&A getting done at a 4.99% 10-year, but leveraged loan buyers are picky. Brent near $114 keeps energy dealmaking active.

pitch: Stocks rose again on Tuesday. The S&P gained about 0.6 percent and the Nasdaq 1.2, led by chips as Anthropic's IPO filing revived the AI trade. Oil slipped about 2 percent on Middle East talks, but Brent at roughly 114 dollars is still near six-month highs. The 10-year ended at 4.99 percent, and the Fed decides Wednesday with about a 90 percent chance of a hold at 3.75 to 4. On M&A, HealthSpan agreed to buy Surgery Partners for about 5.7 billion dollars, and EQT is buying Range Resources in an all-stock deal. Credit is open but selective.

quiz.q: Where did the 10-year Treasury close on Tuesday 27 Oct?
Why did oil fall on Tuesday 27 Oct?
quiz.a: Diplomacy involving Iran and regional powers eased Middle East supply fears, though prices stayed near six-month highs.
options: Middle East talks eased supply fears

quiz.q: Who was the exclusive financial adviser to HealthSpan on its Surgery Partners deal?
quiz.a: Jefferies, which also committed the financing.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: Brent settled at $113.88 and WTI at $99.90 on Tuesday, each down about 2% on Middle East talks, but both are near six-month highs. Houthi attacks and Hormuz disruption keep a risk premium in. High prices support producer cash flow, which helps funding for energy M&A like EQT-Range.

HealthSpan agreed to buy Surgery Partners for about $5.7B EV in cash at $23.50 a share, with Bain Capital rolling its stake. Jefferies advised HealthSpan and provided financing; Centerview and Leerink advised Surgery Partners. EQT-Range is the energy one, an all-stock deal over $50B pro forma EV.

chat.q: What are you watching this week?
chat.a: The Fed on Wednesday, where markets give about a 90% chance of a hold at 3.75–4.00%. Then Microsoft and Alphabet earnings for AI capex, and Thursday's GDP and core PCE. Those set the rate backdrop for financing.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The discount rate rises, so present value falls, and terminal value falls most because it is the longest-dated cash flow. With the 10-year already at 4.99%, another 50 bp would pressure long-duration equity values and make leveraged buyouts harder to finance.
chat.tip: State direction, then the terminal value point.

chat.q: Why would EQT pay in stock for Range?
chat.a: An all-stock deal avoids new borrowing when the 10-year is 4.99% and credit is selective. Range holders get about 27% of the combined company and share in roughly $325M of base synergies expected within two years. The tradeoff is dilution and two shareholder votes.

chat.q: How would you describe credit markets today?
chat.a: Open but selective. The latest FRED reading, from 26 Oct, showed high yield at 330 bp and investment grade at 90 bp, tight by history. Octus reported weaker deals were pulled or restructured, such as AVI-SPL's $690M loan, while Crescent Energy's $1.5B term loan priced.
chat.tip: Give both sides: tight spreads, picky buyers.
